lessons.evidence: v_5ba7effa only, 4 pulls cumulative: 2,022 impressions, 72 clicks, CTR 3.56%, 5 conversions, spend $215.84, CPA $43.17. Pull 4 alone: 658 impressions, 22 clicks (about 3.34% CTR), 2 conversions, $65.95 spend (about $32.98 CPA). CTR is still the second highest of the valid variants and has held between about 3.3% and 3.7% across all four pulls. CPA improved from $49.96 (3 pulls) to $43.17 but is still the highest or near-highest, and rests on 5 conversions (single digits). v_test_zerospend (also open-house) is excluded in memory by person decision (round 2) as a tracking error (2 conversions, $0 spend) and is not counted here.
lessons.recommendation: Do not call a winner or loser. CTR strength looks real and CPA is trending toward the pack, but 5 conversions is too few; need roughly 10+ conversions across more pulls before judging whether the CTR converts to affordable CPA.

lessons.evidence: Re-tagged from walk-to-transit to trail-access by person decision (round 2), because the creative is about the Willowmere Lake walking trail, not transit. v_23990f50 only, 4 pulls cumulative: 2,332 impressions, 57 clicks, CTR 2.44%, 4 conversions, spend $133.80, CPA $33.45. Pull 4 alone: 814 impressions, 16 clicks (about 1.97% CTR), 1 conversion at about $37.56. CTR has slipped from 2.70% to 2.44% and CPA has drifted upward from $23.47 to $30.52 to $32.08 to $33.45 as conversions accrued. Only 4 conversions, so CPA is noisy.
lessons.recommendation: No decision on 4 pulls. Tag matches the creative. Do not run a transit angle: the listing sheet has no approved transit facts. No scale or pause call before 10+ conversions per variant (person decision, round 2). Mid-pack on CPA, below average on CTR; keep watching the CTR slide.

lessons.evidence: v_78931fb8, 4 pulls cumulative: 2,797 impressions, 93 clicks, CTR 3.32%, 9 conversions, spend $231.83, CPA $25.76. Pull 4 alone: 746 impressions, 30 clicks (about 4.02% CTR), 3 conversions, $74.78 spend (about $24.93 CPA). Lowest or near-lowest CPA of the valid variants at every pull, and the lead has now held for four pulls. 9 conversions is still single digits, one short of the 10+ threshold. Second creative v_7f691c4d, 2 pulls cumulative: 960 impressions, 35 clicks, CTR 3.65%, 4 conversions, spend $89.83, CPA $22.46 (pull 2 alone: 564 impressions, 20 clicks, 2 conversions at about $25.67, in line with pull 1, so no spike). Two creatives pointing the same direction is encouraging, but v_7f691c4d is on 2 pulls and 4 conversions, so it is not yet confirmation; the two creatives are not pooled.
lessons.recommendation: Best CPA so far and the lead is consistent across four pulls and two creatives, but not confirmed. Keep collecting; do not scale until v_78931fb8 passes 10+ conversions and v_7f691c4d gets more pulls and conversions. Likely to merit a confidence upgrade to medium at the next pull if the CPA holds. Need at least 2 more pulls on v_7f691c4d before comparing the two low-hoa creatives (angle vs. specific variant test).

lessons.evidence: v_c3aa75c1 only, 4 pulls cumulative: 2,640 impressions, 68 clicks, CTR 2.58%, 4 conversions, spend $179.76, CPA $44.94. Pull 4 alone: 425 impressions, 10 clicks (about 2.35% CTR), 1 conversion at about $26.44. CPA improved from $51.11 but rests on 4 conversions, and the improvement is from a single conversion, so it is noisy. Highest impressions and spend among the original five; CPA still near open-house.
lessons.recommendation: No decision on 4 pulls. Mid-to-low CTR with high CPA is a pattern to watch; continue collecting before comparing against other angles.

lessons.evidence: v_45b12395 only, 4 pulls cumulative: 2,202 impressions, 32 clicks, CTR 1.45% (lowest of the valid variants at every pull; pull 4 alone about 1.3%: 304 impressions, 4 clicks), 0 conversions, spend $60.81, CPA null. Consistent with weak performance across four pulls, but 0 conversions on 32 clicks is still thin to call a loser. Its HOA content overlaps the low-hoa variants, which are the stronger framing so far.
lessons.recommendation: Do not drop on 4 pulls with 0 conversions. Lowest CTR, no conversions and lowest spend make it the first candidate for a person to pause if budget needs freeing, but a loser call needs more clicks and pulls.
